stem: An alert 6-year-old child weighing 27 kg develops a blood glucose level of 3.8 mmol/L during treatment for diabetic ketoacidosis and can safely take oral carbohydrate. What oral treatment amount is recommended?
explanation: 10 g high-GI carbohydrate is the recommended oral treatment amount for a child older than 5 years or heavier than 25 kg who can safely take oral carbohydrate.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because 2 g is below the recommended oral treatment dose.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 5 g is used for younger or lighter children, not for this child.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because children older than 5 years or weighing more than 25 kg are given 10 g high-GI carbohydrate if they can safely take oral treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 15 g is not the recommended oral treatment amount in this situation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 20 g is not the recommended oral treatment amount in this situation.
